answer: Each identity locks 250 units and registers an output pigment — a compact fingerprint of replies to a hidden prompt set. New entries sit in a quarantine lagoon for three epochs while the catalog is searched; a collision, or a later missed live challenge, slashes the deposit and retires the key. Secret prompts each epoch must match that fingerprint. An attacker cannot wander one model across many names because clones collide and burn; each extra identity needs its own trained or fine-tuned model plus a fresh locked deposit, so farm cost scales with distinct models, not cheap keygen.
